title: General Tso's-Style Baked Chicken
seoTitle: General Tso's-Style Baked Chicken | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Crispy oven-baked chicken with a sweet-spicy chili glaze baked right in
subtitle: Crispy oven-baked chicken with a sweet-spicy chili glaze baked right in
description: Chicken thigh chunks get a light cornstarch coating and bake until crisp-edged, then get brushed with a glossy General Tso's-style glaze built on dried chilies, hoisin, garlic, and ginger and baked again until the sauce sets into the coating, served over rice with broccoli.

steps.title: Coat and bake the chicken
steps.instruction: Toss chicken chunks in beaten egg, then dredge in ¼ cup cornstarch. Arrange on a well-oiled sheet pan with space between pieces. Bake at 425°F 22–25 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden and crisp-edged.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.instruction: Rinse and cook jasmine rice per package directions; fluff and hold covered while the chicken bakes.

steps.title: Make the glaze
steps.instruction: Combine soy sauce, hoisin, vinegar, brown sugar, and remaining cornstarch in a saucepan. Add dried chilies, garlic, and ginger, simmer 5–6 minutes, whisking, until thickened and glossy enough to coat a spoon thickly (thicker than a tossing glaze—this one gets brushed on and baked).

steps.title: Steam the broccoli
steps.instruction: Steam broccoli florets 4–5 minutes until bright green and just fork-tender.

steps.title: Glaze and bake again
steps.instruction: Brush the glaze generously over the baked chicken right on the sheet pan. Return to the oven 6–8 minutes until the glaze sets into a sticky, caramelized coating instead of sitting wet on top. Top with scallions, serve over rice with broccoli alongside.

proTips: The dried chilies are for aroma more than eating—warn the crew not to bite into them whole.
A wire rack on the sheet pan crisps the chicken on all sides, not just the bottom.
Reduce dried chilies to 3 for a milder, more kid-friendly version at home.
leftovers: Reheat in the oven or air fryer—the baked-in glaze holds up far better than a tossed-on sauce would.
Chop into fried rice the next night with leftover rice.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Sweet-heat glaze that's genuinely takeout-shop familiar—more chili-forward than a mild honey-garlic chicken. Baking the glaze on instead of tossing it at the end means it actually holds through a hold-and-reheat instead of going soft.
mealPrepNotes: Spread chicken pieces with real space on the sheet pan so they crisp instead of steam. Station: Flip chicken halfway through the first bake for even browning on all sides. Station: Brush the glaze on and bake again briefly so it sets into the coating rather than sitting wet on top—this is what makes it hold and reheat well. Station: Steam broccoli while the chicken bakes so everything finishes together.

adaptable.label: Gluten-Free Adaptable
adaptable.note: Use tamari (check soy-free brands separately) or coconut aminos. Use a certified gluten-free hoisin or a tamari-based substitute.
